task_instance: Review a sample Salesforce after-save Record-Triggered Flow (Opportunity Closed-Won -> update related Contacts) against the skill's checklist (flow-type selection, bulk safety, fault paths, automation density, deployment safety), identify anti-patterns, and produce a corrected Flow metadata XML plus a written review report.
tools_used: Bash (python3 xml.dom.minidom for well-formedness check, grep)
evidence: Created Opportunity_Update_Related_Contacts.flow-original.xml containing a deliberately flawed after-save Record-Triggered Flow (DML 'Update Records' element inside a Loop, and no fault connectors on the Get Records or Update Records elements). Applied the skill's Step 1-7 checklist in review-report.md: confirmed Flow (not formula/validation rule) and After-Save Record-Triggered type were correct choices; flagged the DML-in-loop violation (Step 3, 'Automatic Fail') and the missing fault connectors (Step 4); documented the Automation Density check as an admin action item (Step 5, not resolvable from a static file); noted Screen Flow UX guidelines (Step 6) as N/A; and laid out the Draft->1 record->200+ record->Activate deployment path (Step 7). Produced Opportunity_Update_Related_Contacts.flow-fixed.xml implementing the fixes: the DML update is moved out of the loop to run once in bulk against a collection variable (varContactsToUpdate) populated during the loop via an Assignment element, and faultConnector elements were added on both the Get Records and Update Records elements routing to a Log_Flow_Error record-create element. Verified both original and fixed XML files are well-formed via `python3 -c "import xml.dom.minidom as m; m.parse(f)"` (both printed 'well-formed OK'), and confirmed via grep that the fixed file contains exactly the expected faultConnector blocks and that the recordUpdates element appears once outside the loop. Files produced: /tmp/.../Opportunity_Update_Related_Contacts.flow-original.xml, /tmp/.../Opportunity_Update_Related_Contacts.flow-fixed.xml, /tmp/.../review-report.md. This fully exercises the skill's core deliverable (a Flow design review that catches bulk-safety and fault-handling violations and produces a corrected design) using only local file authoring and shell/XML validation, with no external Salesforce org, credentials, or paid service required.
